key_insight: A synthetic, spanwise-uniform large-scale structure imposed in the outer layer can directly modulate near-wall turbulence in a turbulent boundary layer through phase-dependent top-down interactions.
engineering_relevance: This suggests outer-layer actuation can be used to study, and potentially control, boundary-layer turbulence dynamics and wall-shear-related behavior in flow-control applications.
method: Active plasma actuator placed in the outer region to generate a periodic synthetic large-scale structure.
Planar particle image velocimetry and spanwise-offset hot-wires measured downstream response over a long streamwise extent.
Phase-locked analysis isolated large-scale motion development and turbulence-amplitude modulation.
evidence_signal: Experiments showed strong correlation between near-wall large-scale motions and periodic turbulence-amplitude modulation, with phase-dependent changes in production and transport, plus transient changes in spanwise coherence.
watch_item: The induced near-wall effects were intermittent and transient, so the response may not translate to sustained control in more complex or higher-Reynolds-number flows.
paper_title: Response of a Turbulent Boundary Layer to a Synthetic Periodic Large-Scale Structure
